changes: Delete explanatory comment deviations;restore original surrounding comments and logical lines. No executable expression or binding changed.

points.evidence: Original WWS32WSAUnhookBlockingHook tests the WSAIsBlocking function pointer instead of invoking it. The loaded non-null entry therefore always returns WSAEINPROGRESS. WWS32WSASetBlockingHook and WWS32WSACleanup correctly invoke the same provider predicate. Restoring that pointer test reintroduces deterministic false rejection.

Original WWS32WSACleanup decrements per-task startup count and calls WWS32TaskCleanup at zero while the task remains alive. Native WSAStartup is process-wide; the original task cleanup frees TLS-owned buffers and sockets without cancelling task-owned async contexts. The new early task-exit binding cannot replace explicit WSACleanup. Existing single-list owner-qualified retirement must remain at this shared cleanup entry.
